model.name: UK Cyber Essentials (starter)
model.documentation: The five technical control themes of Cyber Essentials, the UK government-backed scheme run by the National Cyber Security Centre, each realized by example controls that are applied to the in-scope estate: network boundary, end user devices, servers and cloud services. It follows Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3 (April 2026); Cyber Essentials Plus assesses the same requirements with hands-on technical verification. Requirements are paraphrased; the NCSC document is the reference. Replace the example professional services firm's estate with your own asset register: every in-scope device and cloud service needs each theme that applies to it covered by a control.

element.name: Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3
element.documentation: Published by the NCSC in April 2026. Certification is awarded by a Certification Body against an agreed scope.

element.name: Protection against common internet-based attacks
element.documentation: Prevent the large majority of commodity cyber attacks: phishing, password guessing, and exploitation of known vulnerabilities and default settings.

element.name: Agreed scope boundary
element.documentation: The whole IT infrastructure, or a separately managed sub-set, defined by business unit, network boundary and physical location and agreed with the Certification Body. End user devices must be included, and cloud services that hold organisational data or services can never be excluded.

element.name: In scope
element.documentation: Devices and services that can accept inbound connections from the internet, make outbound connections over it, or control data flows between the two.

element.name: Out of scope
element.documentation: Excluded by the scheme's scope rules. Record why each item is out of scope; the assessor will ask.

element.name: Home broadband routers not supplied by the firm
element.documentation: Out of scope. Laptops used at home rely on their software firewall instead.

element.name: Phones used only for calls, texts and MFA apps
element.documentation: Out of scope: devices used only for native voice, native text or MFA applications.

element.name: Bespoke code of the client portal
element.documentation: Out of scope: bespoke and custom web application components. Covered by secure development practice.

element.name: Firewalls
element.documentation: Every in-scope device sits behind a correctly configured boundary or software firewall. Default administrator passwords are changed, the administration interface is not reachable from the internet without a documented need and MFA or an IP allow list, unauthenticated inbound connections are blocked by default, and every inbound rule is approved, documented with its business need and removed when no longer needed.

element.name: Software firewalls on laptops
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this theme in your organisation.

element.name: Secure configuration
element.documentation: Unnecessary accounts and software are removed or disabled, default or guessable passwords are changed, auto-run is disabled, users are authenticated before reaching organisational data or services, and devices lock with a PIN, password or biometric protected against brute force.

element.name: Hardened standard builds

element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this theme in your organisation.

element.name: Security update management
element.documentation: All software is licensed and supported, unsupported software is removed or isolated, automatic updates are on where possible, and updates fixing critical or high risk vulnerabilities (CVSS v3 7 or above, or unrated by the vendor) are applied within 14 days of release.

element.name: Security updates within 14 days
element.documentation: Example control. Replace with the process or tool that meets this theme in your organisation.

element.name: User access control
element.documentation: Accounts are created through an approval process, use unique credentials, are removed when no longer needed and carry only the privileges the role needs. Administrative work uses separate accounts, MFA is used wherever available and is always used for cloud services, and passwords are protected against guessing.

element.name: Malware protection
element.documentation: Every in-scope device runs an active, up-to-date malware protection mechanism: anti-malware software that blocks malicious code and websites, or application allow-listing that only lets approved, signed applications run.

view.documentation: Each technical control theme with the example controls that realize it. Fill in the owner and evidence location of every control: the assessment questions ask for exactly this.

view.documentation: Each control and the part of the estate it is applied to. Every device and cloud service in a category must be covered by the controls drawn to that category; one left out is the finding an assessor raises.
